Threat (short): OMV admin interface compromised via default or weak credentials
Requirement: No default passwords (SR-01). Admin interface limited to LAN and VPN, HTTPS (SR-02). Separate admin and daily accounts, sudo for admin only (SR-03)
Control implemented: Default OMV password changed. Separate administration, daily, monitoring and Claude Code accounts. OMV over HTTPS with HTTP redirect (D-04). Admin interface reached only on the LAN and over Tailscale
Baseline result: V-13 Fail: default OMV admin password in use (FND-01, treated). V-12: one account for administration and daily use, with sudo (FND-05)
Post-hardening result: V-13 Pass (4th November 2026, final check confirmed by the owner, 9th November 2026): default login refused. V-12 Pass (4th and 6th November 2026): only the administration account has sudo. V-20, V-21, V-24 Pass

Threat (short): Known vulnerability exploited in OMV / Debian / exposed service
Requirement: Only inventoried services listen (SR-07). Updates within the routine (SR-10). Vulnerability check every 12 hours (SR-14)
Control implemented: rpcbind, LLMNR, Avahi, Bluetooth, WS-Discovery and SMB port 139 off. Automatic Debian security updates, written update routine (D-08). Vulnerability dashboard with KEV check (D-03)
Baseline result: V-01: 22, 80, 111 and 5355 open. V-03: SSH 10.x, nginx version hidden, OMV update pending (FND-06). V-05: hardening index 63. V-10: no security updates pending
Post-hardening result: V-01 Pass (final check, 9th November 2026): only 22, 80 (redirect to HTTPS only), 443 and 445 open. V-04 Pass (6th November 2026): SMB on 445 only, nothing unexplained. V-03 Pass (final check, 9th November 2026). V-10 Pass (final check, 9th November 2026): no pending security update, 10 other updates less than 14 days old, due by 20th November 2026 (D-08). V-18 Pass. V-05 Pass (owner, 9th November 2026): hardening index 67 (Phase 0: 63), only the baseline false-positive warning

Threat (short): Accidental internet exposure of a NAS service
Requirement: No port forwards, DMZ or UPnP (SR-08). No NAS service reachable from the internet over IPv4 or IPv6 (SR-09)
Control implemented: UPnP turned off (FND-07 treated). No port forwards or DMZ host. Remote access through Tailscale only
Baseline result: V-07: no port forwards, no DMZ, UPnP on with no mappings (FND-07), not behind CGNAT. V-08 IPv4: only 7547 open on the public address, on the router, most likely the ISP's TR-069 management, risk accepted (FND-09). The other four ports came from the mobile network. V-08 IPv6: all ports filtered on both NAS addresses, through a VPN, not confirmed with tcpdump. Router: no IPv6 pinholes
Post-hardening result: V-07 Pass (3rd November 2026): UPnP off after a router restart. Final check (owner, 9th November 2026): no port forwards, UPnP off. V-08 Pass (owner, 8th November 2026): all 65,535 TCP ports filtered on the home public IPv4 address and both NAS IPv6 addresses, through a commercial VPN, 7th November 2026. Port 7547 did not answer on the current address. FND-09 acceptance unchanged. V-23 Pass (owner, same scan). Phase 2: no port forward added, as Tailscale was kept (D-16, D-19), so SR-08 and SR-09 are still met in their Phase 1 form
Evidence: evidence/phase0/V-08_external-scan.txt; V-08_external-scan-ipv6-1-rerun.txt; V-08_external-scan-ipv6-2-rerun.txt; evidence/phase1/V-08_external-services-vpn.txt; evidence/phase1/V-08_external-scan-ipv4.txt; V-08_external-scan-ipv6-1.txt; V-08_external-scan-ipv6-2.txt; V-08_control-ipv4.txt; V-08_control-ipv6.txt
